question: A team in a regulated industry is setting up a Claude Project to draft client onboarding letters. Which sequence best follows a typical organisational AI policy?
options: A) Confirm the use case and data types are permitted; get the data owner's approval; upload the material and set project instructions; pilot with a named human reviewer.
B) Upload the material and set project instructions; pilot with a named human reviewer; confirm the use case and data types are permitted; get the data owner's approval.
C) Upload the material and set project instructions; confirm the use case and data types are permitted; get the data owner's approval; pilot with a named human reviewer.
D) Get the data owner's approval; upload the material and set project instructions; confirm the use case and data types are permitted; pilot with a named human reviewer.
correct_answers: A) Confirm the use case and data types are permitted; get the data owner's approval; upload the material and set project instructions; pilot with a named human reviewer.
explanations: Correct. Policy questions come before data moves: establish that the use and the data classes are allowed, obtain the owner's approval, then configure, then prove it works under human review.
This puts client material into the workspace before anyone has confirmed the use case is permitted, which is the step the policy exists to prevent.
Uploading first means the data is already in the workspace while the permission question is still open.
Approval cannot be sought sensibly before the use case itself has been confirmed as permitted, and configuration still precedes that confirmation here.
